text: Erling Norvik (9 April 1928 – 31 December 1998) was a Norwegian politician affiliated with the Conservative Party. He was born in Vadsø and is the son of Erling Johannes Norvik, who served in the Norwegian parliament (Stortinget) from 1949 to 1961. The younger Norvik began his professional career as a journalist for the regional newspaper Finnmarken at the age of 12 and was elected to Stortinget in 1961 from Finnmark, succeeding his father. He served in the legislature for three consecutive terms from 1961 to 1973, after which he resigned to become the leader of the Conservative Party, a position he held from 1974 to 1980 and again from 1984 to 1986. In 1981, he declined a ministerial appointment and instead worked in the prime minister's office of his party colleague Kåre Willoch. In 1986, he was appointed Governor ("Fylkesmann") of Østfold county, a role he held for 12 years. This article about a Norwegian politician born in the 1920s is a stub.
